A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlowCut study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original FlowCut benchmark evaluations, inference and training efficiency measurements, component ablations, and information-flow analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds benchmark comparisons, a 32-token evaluation, and hyperparameter sensitivity experiments in Tables 8–11.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains entropy-adaptive pruning, the same three importance criteria, 0.5/0.5 cumulative scoring, and pruning every two layers. The new implementation discussion and pseudocode do not establish a change to the tested algorithm.

E1.justification: Table 9 adds AI2D and MMMU evaluations to the retained image/video benchmark coverage through the ST3 comparison. The 32-token experiment reuses existing datasets and changes the token budget rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 9 substantially expands the evaluated comparator set with LLaVA-PruMerge, VTW, RCom, FasterVLM, and ST3. The original comparisons remain. CrossGET is newly discussed but has no reported comparative results, so it is not an added evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The supplementary experiments introduce a 32-token budget and a comparison following ST3's benchmark protocol, reporting 4.25 TFLOPs for FlowCut versus 4.27 for ST3. Additional controlled settings vary accumulation weights and pruning intervals; the original inference and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds systematic POPE sensitivity analyses of two previously fixed design choices: historical/current score weights and pruning frequency. Tables 10–11 compare these sweeps against non-cumulative and final-layer-only controls, substantially extending the existing component ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark performance. The added tables continue reporting point estimates, and the existing value-vector distribution boxplots are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 8–11 add substantial comparative and sensitivity results, including 90.8% relative average performance for FlowCut at 32 tokens versus VisionZip's 88.7%. Table 6 also corrects nine 192-token relative percentages, including GQA from 98.1% to 100.2% and MMVet from 103.5% to 108.0%; its raw scores and overall 101.1% average remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a limited complexity argument: separately computing the CLS/global token's 1-by-N attention requires O(N) auxiliary computation. The information-flow definitions and Equations 1–6 otherwise retain their mathematical substance; Equation 4's information-density symbol correction is not a new definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, main contributions, and conclusion retain the same information-flow explanation, pruning framework, and headline efficiency/performance claims. The revised first contribution bullet restates the unified, bottom-up perspective already present in v1.

C2.justification: The new sensitivity discussion interprets the results as robustness to weighting and pruning frequency, and attributes pruning every layer's slightly lower performance to missing historical scores at the first pruning step. Existing redundancy and hallucination interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds implementation pseudocode and explains FlashAttention compatibility through separate CLS/global-token attention computation. Hardware and code-access disclosures remain substantially unchanged. The pseudocode introduces an inconsistency: it labels Equation 3's pruning count as a ratio and uses it in round((1-prune_ratio)*N), limiting its reproducibility value.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds fourteen works, and Appendix A.3 substantially expands discussion of competing token-compression methods. It explicitly distinguishes FlowCut from CrossGET's learnable cross tokens and retraining requirements, extending substantive positioning beyond the original comparisons with FastV, SparseVLM, VisionZip, and PDrop.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order remain intact. Changes include a rewritten contribution bullet, acknowledgments and author/header updates, and three new appendix subsections; Broader Impact and More Visualization Results move from A.3–A.4 to A.6–A.7.

P2.justification: The appendix gains four experimental tables, including side-by-side comparator panels and two sensitivity-sweep layouts, plus the substantial Algorithm 1 display. Existing Figures 1–11 retain identical image content, and the main table structures remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: Additional competitor comparisons and POPE sensitivity tests strengthen empirical support, while Table 6's corrected percentages restore numerical consistency. These gains support a limited overall improvement, tempered by Algorithm 1's new count-versus-fraction error, which makes the added pseudocode unreliable as written.
